title: Quantum Relative Entropy, Data Processing, and Strong Subadditivity

items.title: Inverse compression for a positive operator
items.statement:
Let $H,K$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces, with inner products linear in the first argument. Let $V:H\to K$ be a linear isometry, let $T:K\to K$ be positive definite, and let $s\ge0$. Then
$$V^\dagger(T+sI_K)^{-1}V\succeq(V^\dagger TV+sI_H)^{-1},$$
where $A\succeq B$ means $A-B$ is nonnegative.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018), Chapter 5, §§5.2.1, 5.2.3, and Theorem 5.49
references.locator: §§5.2.1 and 5.2.3, printed pp. 266–282; §5.3, Holevo’s theorem, printed pp. 295–300.

references.title: Mark M. Wilde, From Classical to Quantum Shannon Theory, second-edition prepublication v8 (2019)
references.locator: Chapter 11, §§11.8–11.9.2, printed pp. 339–352 (PDF pages 340–352).

items.title: The resolvent proof of the compression inequality for minus the logarithm
items.statement:
Let $T$ be a positive-definite endomorphism of a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space $K$, and let $V:H\to K$ be an isometry from a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space. Define $\log T$ by the natural logarithm of the positive eigenvalues in the finite spectral decomposition. Then
$$-\log(V^\dagger TV)\preceq V^\dagger(-\log T)V.$$

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018), Chapter 5, §§5.2.1, 5.2.3, and Theorem 5.49
references.locator: §§5.2.1 and 5.2.3, printed pp. 266–282; §5.3, Holevo’s theorem, printed pp. 295–300.

references.title: Mark M. Wilde, From Classical to Quantum Shannon Theory, second-edition prepublication v8 (2019)
references.locator: Chapter 11, §§11.8–11.9.2, printed pp. 339–352 (PDF pages 340–352).

items.title: The finite relative-modular operator identity
items.statement:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space with inner product linear in its first argument, and let $A,B\in\operatorname{End}(H)$ be positive definite. Equip $\operatorname{End}(H)$ with $\langle X,Y\rangle_{HS}:=\operatorname{tr}(XY^\dagger)$, define $L_B(X)=BX$ and $R_{A^{-1}}(X)=XA^{-1}$, and put $\Delta_{B,A}=L_BR_{A^{-1}}$. Then $\Delta_{B,A}$ is positive definite and
$$\langle(-\log\Delta_{B,A})A^{1/2},A^{1/2}\rangle_{HS}=D(A\Vert B).$$
All logarithms are the natural spectral logarithms on positive eigenvalues.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018), Chapter 5, §§5.2.1, 5.2.3, and Theorem 5.49
references.locator: §§5.2.1 and 5.2.3, printed pp. 266–282; §5.3, Holevo’s theorem, printed pp. 295–300.

references.title: Mark M. Wilde, From Classical to Quantum Shannon Theory, second-edition prepublication v8 (2019)
references.locator: Chapter 11, §§11.8–11.9.2, printed pp. 339–352 (PDF pages 340–352).

items.title: Support-sensitive regularization limit for quantum relative entropy
items.statement:
For non-negative $A,B$ on a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space,

$$\lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}D(A+\varepsilon I\|B+\varepsilon I)=D(A\|B),$$

where the right side may be $+\infty$ under the support convention of [[def-it-finite-dimensional-quantum-relative-entropy]].

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, §§5.2.1 and 5.2.3
Mark M. Wilde, From Classical to Quantum Shannon Theory, §11.8

items.title: Joint convexity of finite-dimensional quantum relative entropy
items.statement:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space. For a finite family of positive semidefinite operators $A_i,B_i$ on $H$ and weights $\lambda_i\ge0$ with $\sum_i\lambda_i=1$,
$$D\!\left(\sum_i\lambda_iA_i\middle\Vert\sum_i\lambda_iB_i\right)\le\sum_i\lambda_iD(A_i\Vert B_i),$$
where $D$ is the support-sensitive extended quantum relative entropy and zero-weight terms are omitted.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018), Chapter 5, §§5.2.1, 5.2.3, and Theorem 5.49
references.locator: §§5.2.1 and 5.2.3, printed pp. 266–282; §5.3, Holevo’s theorem, printed pp. 295–300.

references.title: Mark M. Wilde, From Classical to Quantum Shannon Theory, second-edition prepublication v8 (2019)
references.locator: Chapter 11, §§11.8–11.9.2, printed pp. 339–352 (PDF pages 340–352).

items.title: The finite Weyl twirl is the normalized partial trace
items.statement:
Let $H,K$ be finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces with $d=\dim K\ge1$, and fix an ordered orthonormal basis $e_0,\ldots,e_{d-1}$ of $K$. Let $X e_j=e_{j+1\,\mathrm{mod}\,d}$ and $Z e_j=\omega^j e_j$, where $\omega=\exp(2\pi i/d)$ (and $\omega=1$ when $d=1$). For $R\in\operatorname{End}(H\otimes K)$,
$$\frac1{d^2}\sum_{p,q=0}^{d-1}(I_H\otimes X^pZ^q)R(I_H\otimes X^pZ^q)^\dagger=(\operatorname{Tr}_K R)\otimes I_K/d.$$

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018), Chapter 5, §§5.2.1, 5.2.3, and Theorem 5.49
references.locator: §§5.2.1 and 5.2.3, printed pp. 266–282; §5.3, Holevo’s theorem, printed pp. 295–300.

references.title: Mark M. Wilde, From Classical to Quantum Shannon Theory, second-edition prepublication v8 (2019)
references.locator: Chapter 11, §§11.8–11.9.2, printed pp. 339–352 (PDF pages 340–352).

items.title: Isometric invariance of finite quantum relative entropy
items.statement:
Let $V:H\to K$ be a linear map between finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces satisfying $V^*V=I_H$, and let $A,B$ be non-negative on $H$. Then

$$D(VAV^*\|VBV^*)=D(A\|B).$$

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, Proposition 5.19
Mark M. Wilde, From Classical to Quantum Shannon Theory, Exercise 11.8.6

items.title: Data processing of finite quantum relative entropy under partial trace
items.statement:
Let $H,K$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces with $d=\dim K\ge1$, and let $A,B$ be positive semidefinite endomorphisms of $H\otimes K$. Then
$$D(\operatorname{Tr}_K A\Vert\operatorname{Tr}_K B)\le D(A\Vert B),$$
with the extended support convention.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018), Chapter 5, §§5.2.1, 5.2.3, and Theorem 5.49
references.locator: §§5.2.1 and 5.2.3, printed pp. 266–282; §5.3, Holevo’s theorem, printed pp. 295–300.

references.locator: Chapter 11, §§11.8–11.9.2, printed pp. 339–352 (PDF pages 340–352).

items.title: Data processing for finite-dimensional quantum relative entropy
items.statement:
Let $H,K$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces, let $\Phi:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$ be a quantum channel, and let $A,B\in\mathcal L(H)$ be positive semidefinite. Then
$$D(\Phi(A)\Vert\Phi(B))\le D(A\Vert B),$$
with the support-sensitive extended value convention.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018), Chapter 5, §§5.2.1, 5.2.3, and Theorem 5.49
references.locator: §§5.2.1 and 5.2.3, printed pp. 266–282; §5.3, Holevo’s theorem, printed pp. 295–300.

items.title: Strong subadditivity of finite-dimensional quantum entropy
items.statement:
Let $H_A,H_B,H_C$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let $\rho_{ABC}$ be a density operator on their ordered tensor product. Write $\rho_{AB},\rho_{BC},\rho_B$ for its marginals using the partial traces in [[def-qc-partial-trace]]. Then
$$S(\rho_{AB})+S(\rho_{BC})\ge S(\rho_B)+S(\rho_{ABC}),$$
where $S(\rho)=-\operatorname{tr}(\rho\ln\rho)$ with $0\ln0:=0$ as in [[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]].

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018), Chapter 5, §§5.2.1, 5.2.3, and Theorem 5.49
references.locator: §§5.2.1 and 5.2.3, printed pp. 266–282; §5.3, Holevo’s theorem, printed pp. 295–300.

references.title: Mark M. Wilde, From Classical to Quantum Shannon Theory, second-edition prepublication v8 (2019)
references.locator: Chapter 11, §§11.8–11.9.2, printed pp. 339–352 (PDF pages 340–352).

items.title: Nonnegativity of finite-dimensional quantum conditional mutual information
items.statement:
Let $\rho_{ABC}$ be a finite-dimensional tripartite state, with conditional mutual information defined by [[def-it-finite-quantum-information-measures]]. Then
$$I(A:B\mid C)_\rho=S(\rho_{AC})+S(\rho_{BC})-S(\rho_C)-S(\rho_{ABC})\ge0.$$

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018), Chapter 5, §§5.2.1, 5.2.3, and Theorem 5.49
references.locator: §§5.2.1 and 5.2.3, printed pp. 266–282; §5.3, Holevo’s theorem, printed pp. 295–300.

references.locator: Chapter 11, §§11.8–11.9.2, printed pp. 339–352 (PDF pages 340–352).

items.title: A finite POVM defines a finite quantum-to-classical channel
items.statement:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex-inner-product space and let $(M_y)_{y\in Y}$ be a finite POVM with finite nonempty outcome set $Y$. Let $K=\mathbb C^Y$ have its orthonormal outcome basis $|y\rangle$. Then
$$\mathcal M(X):=\sum_{y\in Y}\operatorname{tr}(M_yX)|y\rangle\langle y|,$$
defines a finite-dimensional quantum channel $\mathcal M:\mathcal L(H)\to\mathcal L(K)$.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018), Chapter 5, §§5.2.1, 5.2.3, and Theorem 5.49
references.locator: §§5.2.1 and 5.2.3, printed pp. 266–282; §5.3, Holevo’s theorem, printed pp. 295–300.

references.title: Mark M. Wilde, From Classical to Quantum Shannon Theory, second-edition prepublication v8 (2019)
references.locator: Chapter 11, §§11.8–11.9.2, printed pp. 339–352 (PDF pages 340–352).

items.title: The finite Holevo measurement bound
items.statement:
Let $X$ be a finite nonempty set, let $(p_x)$ be a probability vector, let $\rho_x$ be density operators on a nonzero finite-dimensional space $H_B$, and let $\bar\rho:=\sum_xp_x\rho_x$. For a finite POVM $(E_y)_{y\in Y}$ on $H_B$, define $w(y\mid x):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_xE_y)$, $q_y:=\sum_xp_xw(y\mid x)$, and the classical mutual information

$$I(X:Y):=\sum_{x,y:p_xw(y\mid x)>0}p_xw(y\mid x)\ln\frac{w(y\mid x)}{q_y}.$$

Then

$$I(X:Y)\le\chi(\{p_x,\rho_x\})=S(\bar\rho)-\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_xS(\rho_x).$$

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018), Chapter 5, §§5.2.1, 5.2.3, and Theorem 5.49
references.locator: §§5.2.1 and 5.2.3, printed pp. 266–282; §5.3, Holevo’s theorem, printed pp. 295–300.

references.locator: Chapter 11, §§11.8–11.9.2, printed pp. 339–352 (PDF pages 340–352).

title: Quantum Relative Entropy, Data Processing, and Strong Subadditivity — Examples

items.title: Qubit dephasing decreases quantum relative entropy
items.statement:
On the qubit space with computational basis $|0\rangle,|1\rangle$, define the dephasing channel
$$\Delta(X)=|0\rangle\langle0|X|0\rangle\langle0|+|1\rangle\langle1|X|1\rangle\langle1|.$$
For $|+\rangle=(|0\rangle+|1\rangle)/\sqrt2$ and $\rho=|+\rangle\langle+|$, $\sigma=\operatorname{diag}(3/4,1/4)$, one has
$$D(\rho\|\sigma)=\tfrac12\ln(16/3)>\tfrac12\ln(4/3)=D(\Delta(\rho)\|\Delta(\sigma)).$$
For the orthogonal pure states $|+\rangle,| -\rangle=(|0\rangle-|1\rangle)/\sqrt2$, the input relative entropy is $+\infty$, whereas both dephased states equal $I/2$ and their relative entropy is $0$.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018), Chapter 5, §§5.2.1, 5.2.3, and Theorem 5.49
references.locator: §§5.2.1 and 5.2.3, printed pp. 266–282; §5.3, Holevo’s theorem, printed pp. 295–300.

references.title: Mark M. Wilde, From Classical to Quantum Shannon Theory, second-edition prepublication v8 (2019)
references.locator: Chapter 11, §§11.8–11.9.2, printed pp. 339–352 (PDF pages 340–352).

items.title: Strong subadditivity for a pure GHZ tripartite state
items.statement:
For three qubit registers $A,B,C$, let
$$|\mathrm{GHZ}\rangle=(|000\rangle+|111\rangle)/\sqrt2,\qquad \rho_{ABC}=|\mathrm{GHZ}\rangle\langle\mathrm{GHZ}|.$$
Each one-register marginal and each two-register marginal has entropy $\ln2$, while $S(\rho_{ABC})=0$. In particular, for the displayed order,
$$S(\rho_{AB})+S(\rho_{BC})=2\ln2>\ln2=S(\rho_B)+S(\rho_{ABC}),$$
so strong subadditivity is strict.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018), Chapter 5, §§5.2.1, 5.2.3, and Theorem 5.49
references.locator: §§5.2.1 and 5.2.3, printed pp. 266–282; §5.3, Holevo’s theorem, printed pp. 295–300.

references.title: Mark M. Wilde, From Classical to Quantum Shannon Theory, second-edition prepublication v8 (2019)
references.locator: Chapter 11, §§11.8–11.9.2, printed pp. 339–352 (PDF pages 340–352).

items.title: Fidelity and trace-distance inequalities do not imply QRE data processing
items.statement:
Write $\rho_p=\operatorname{diag}(1-p,p)$ for a diagonal qubit state. Set $a=\pi/12$ and
$$\mathcal S_a=\{\rho_{\sin^2\theta}:a\le\theta\le\pi/4\},\qquad T_a(\rho_{\sin^2\theta})=\rho_{\sin^2(\theta-a)}.$$
On this family, $T_a$ preserves root fidelity and contracts trace distance for every pair, but it sends the finite input relative entropy $D(\rho_{\sin^2(\pi/4)}\|\rho_{\sin^2 a})$ to $D(\rho_{\sin^2(\pi/4-a)}\|\rho_0)=+\infty$. The map is nonlinear and is not the restriction of a quantum channel. Thus metric inequalities on a family under an arbitrary map do not by themselves prove quantum-relative-entropy data processing for channels.

As a separate support check, $|0\rangle\langle0|$ and $|+\rangle\langle+|$ have root fidelity and trace distance both $1/\sqrt2$, while $D(|0\rangle\langle0|\| |+\rangle\langle+|)=+\infty$.

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information (2018), Chapter 5, §§5.2.1, 5.2.3, and Theorem 5.49
references.locator: §§5.2.1 and 5.2.3, printed pp. 266–282; §5.3, Holevo’s theorem, printed pp. 295–300.
